take_homes: Ask what would have to be true for someone to drop how they do the job today. They're not competing with nothing.
Plan the people side (who owns, maintains and vouches for it) as seriously as the build. My org-wide setups only have the technical half.
A good agent output still doesn't get used unless the people who decide trust it.

monday.move: Ask one sales lead how they prepare their weekly pipeline review today and what they'd have to see before they'd drop it. I won't build anything before that.
monday.who: A sales lead, probably the one who never opened the licence
monday.stop_condition: If they say they're fine as they are and there's no real pain, I drop the sales setup. I won't push it.
monday.blocker: Nobody outside engineering asked for it, and I haven't found who would maintain it. I'll probably want to build a demo first anyway.

misconception.why: The story shows a good agent-made analysis that nobody acted on, so output quality wasn't the problem. That doesn't change my view on checking agent output, which I'd still skip as a beginner step. It does make me doubt that 'the agent is good' is enough when the goal is adoption.
